- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, leading to prolonged overestimation.
- Model underestimates prices during mean-reversion phases, particularly when prices drop below 65–68.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in downward trends.
- Model exhibits high variance in short-term (1–3 day) predictions, often missing local volatility shifts.
- In high volatility periods, model fails to capture downward momentum, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model tends to underestimate prices during the final 5–7 days of the forecast horizon, possibly due to reduced confidence or model decay.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model overreacts with excessive upward bias, then fails to adjust for subsequent pullback.
